blinding_guess.why: The consumer side is internally consistent at this revision: the FollowPath BT node creates a client for nav2_msgs/action/FollowPath on the hard-coded name follow_path, the bundled BTs do not remap it, and every goal/result field and error-code constant the consumer code reads (path, controller_id, goal_checker_id, progress_checker_id, error_code, NONE, UNKNOWN, PATIENCE_EXCEEDED, FAILED_TO_MAKE_PROGRESS, NO_VALID_CONTROL) exists in the FollowPath.action in the same snapshot. The only irregularity seen is cosmetic Groot metadata (nav2_tree_nodes.xml lists a service_name port for FollowPath while the code uses server_name).

notes: The snapshot is the whole navigation2 repository; the package described is nav2_bt_navigator (node name bt_navigator, package.xml version 1.2.9). bt_navigator consumes follow_path only through the BT plugin library nav2_follow_path_action_bt_node (source in nav2_behavior_tree, same snapshot), which it loads by default via the plugin_lib_names parameter (bt_navigator.cpp:39-94) and which its bundled BT XMLs instantiate as <FollowPath .../>. The action name follow_path is hard-coded in the plugin's registration (follow_path_action.cpp:106; also controller_cancel_node.cpp:42 for the CancelControl node) and can be remapped per BT node by the server_name input port (bt_action_node.hpp:71-75); none of the BT XMLs in nav2_bt_navigator/behavior_trees set server_name. The client is created on the BT client node (named <node>_<action>_rclcpp_node, bt_action_server_impl.hpp:116-130), so the relative name resolves in bt_navigator's namespace. Default BTs: navigate_to_pose_w_replanning_and_recovery.xml and navigate_through_poses_w_replanning_and_recovery.xml (navigate_to_pose.cpp, navigate_through_poses.cpp); both paths are parameters (default_nav_to_pose_bt_xml, default_nav_through_poses_bt_xml) that can be overridden at run time. Goal fields set by the consumer: path, controller_id, goal_checker_id, progress_checker_id (follow_path_action.cpp:33-36); result field read: error_code (follow_path_action.cpp:47); constants used: Goal NONE (follow_path_action.cpp:41,54) and UNKNOWN, PATIENCE_EXCEEDED, FAILED_TO_MAKE_PROGRESS, NO_VALID_CONTROL (would_a_controller_recovery_help_condition.cpp:27-30). FollowPath.action defines the error-code constants in the goal section and has feedback float32 distance_to_goal, float32 speed with no units stated, so units is null. Frame is per_message: the goal carries a nav_msgs/Path whose header frame comes from the blackboard path produced at run time; the consumer does not hard-code a frame for this element. QoS: no QoS is set in code; values are the rcl_action client defaults. An action spans several channels: reliability is RELIABLE on all of them; durability is VOLATILE on the goal, result and cancel services and the feedback topic, but TRANSIENT_LOCAL on the status topic; the single durability field records the goal/feedback channels. Timeouts that bound the client but are not rates: wait_for_service_timeout default 1000 ms, default_server_timeout default 20 ms, bt_loop_duration default 10 ms (bt_action_server_impl.hpp:58-69). No exclusive resources are claimed. declares and not_declared are empty because the only packet element is consumed.
